messages:
nina: Running into a bundler parity problem that breaks our edge sample app. Webpack 5 build works locally but Cloudflare edge throws: "TypeError: Class extends value undefined is not a constructor or null".

nina: App is ESM (type: "module") and imports SDK via `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'`. Repro only when bundling with rollup (used by sample-app tooling) and then running in the edge adapter.

paul: curious, do you have conditional exports? many bundlers mis-handle mixed exports when there are `import` and `require` targets.

nina: package exports snippet: ```"." : { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs", "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" }```

jamie: yep that layout can confuse rollup-plugin-node-resolve depending on the resolver order. Rollup sometimes picks the CJS path then transforms it into ESM wrapper which can break subclassing at runtime.

riley: quick repro I used: 1) init sample app with vite/rollup config from /sample-apps/edge-template, 2) add `@redwood/inference`@0.12.0, 3) `npm run build`, 4) run `wrangler dev` or `miniflare` to emulate CF edge.

nina: workaround: explicit rollup alias to the ESM entry fixed it: `resolve({ alias: { '@redwood/inference': 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.mjs' } })`. But this is a poor onboarding experience.

paul: SDK team should either publish a single unambiguous module field or add an exports fallback that points to ESM for bundlers. Also ensure `types` is accessible without requiring rollup to resolve package exports.

jamie: add CI test: build sample app with rollup+vite and run miniflare smoke to catch this. I'll open a ticket.

deploy-bot: New issue RED-PLAT/SDK#1502 created by jamie: "Rollup resolves CJS wrapper for SDK causing class subclassing error in Cloudflare edge"

nina: I'll add a short note in the sample-app README explaining the alias workaround and include the min steps and a link to the issue.

paul: also try `rollup-plugin-commonjs({ transformMixedEsModules: true })` as an interim relief; it saved me in a previous project.

nina: thanks. Adding the regression test + README patch now.
